subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: An exothermic reaction is one that:
options: Releases heat energy to the surroundings
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions release energy and have a negative enthalpy change (ΔH < 0).

questions.q: The enthalpy change of an endothermic reaction is:
questions.explain: Endothermic reactions absorb energy from the surroundings, giving a positive ΔH.

questions.q: In terms of bonds, an exothermic reaction releases energy overall because:
options: More energy is released making bonds than is absorbed breaking them
More energy is absorbed than released
questions.explain: Bond breaking absorbs energy; bond making releases it. Net release means exothermic.

questions.q: The equation used to calculate heat energy in calorimetry is:
questions.explain: Heat q = mass × specific heat capacity × temperature change.

questions.q: 50 g of water rises by 20 K (c = 4.18 J/g/K). The heat absorbed is approximately:
In a calorimetry experiment, heat lost to the surroundings usually makes the measured enthalpy of combustion:
options: Less exothermic than the true value
More exothermic than the true value
questions.explain: Heat loss means less energy is measured, so the calculated ΔH is smaller in magnitude than the true value.

questions.q: The standard enthalpy change of a reaction is measured under conditions of:
options: 100 kPa and a stated temperature (usually 298 K)
questions.explain: Standard conditions are 100 kPa pressure and a specified temperature, commonly 298 K.

questions.q: If a reaction raises the temperature of its surroundings, the reaction is:
questions.explain: A temperature rise in the surroundings shows energy was released by the reaction.

questions.q: A fuel is best described as a substance that:
questions.explain: Fuels store chemical energy released as heat during combustion.

questions.q: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces:
questions.explain: Complete combustion in plenty of oxygen gives CO2 and H2O.

questions.q: Incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon is a concern because it can produce:
questions.explain: A limited oxygen supply produces poisonous carbon monoxide and soot (carbon).

questions.q: Fossil fuels are described as non-renewable because they:
options: Form over millions of years and are used far faster than they are replaced
questions.explain: Their extremely slow formation means reserves are effectively finite.

questions.q: Biofuels are considered more carbon-neutral than fossil fuels because:
options: The CO2 released was recently absorbed by the plants grown for fuel
questions.explain: Carbon released on burning was recently fixed by photosynthesis, unlike long-stored fossil carbon.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = -890 kJ/mol. This reaction is:
questions.explain: A negative ΔH indicates energy is released to the surroundings.

questions.q: On an energy profile of an exothermic reaction, the products lie:
options: At a lower energy than the reactants
At a higher energy than the reactants
At the same energy as reactants
questions.explain: Energy is released, so products are lower in enthalpy than reactants.

questions.q: Burning 0.50 mol of a fuel releases 400 kJ. The enthalpy of combustion is:
questions.explain: ΔH = -400 kJ ÷ 0.50 mol = -800 kJ/mol (negative because combustion is exothermic).

questions.q: The main greenhouse gas produced by burning fossil fuels is:
questions.explain: Combustion of carbon-based fuels releases CO2, a greenhouse gas.

questions.q: Why is water's high specific heat capacity relevant in calorimetry?
options: A large mass of water changes temperature only slightly for a given heat, so it can absorb reaction heat
It removes the need for insulation
questions.explain: Water is used as the medium to absorb heat, allowing q = mcΔT to be applied.

questions.q: Which produces the most energy per gram on complete combustion, all else equal?
questions.explain: Hydrogen has an exceptionally high energy content per gram, though it is harder to store than carbon-based fuels.

questions.q: Bond breaking is described as an endothermic process because it:
questions.explain: Energy must be supplied to break bonds; forming bonds releases energy.
